description: Demo missions for the ClearGlass Daily Operations Loop. Eight agents across four departments: Executive Suite (Chief of Staff, Risk & Compliance), Engineering Lab (Software Architect, Backend Engineer, QA Engineer), Growth & Marketing Studio (Content Writer, Social Media Agent), Revenue Floor (Lead Research Agent). Values like {"$from": "task", "path": "..."} are filled from an upstream task's output at run time, before the policy engine sees the action.

missions.title: Ship a dependency-aware readiness probe for the Agent Office API
missions.objective: Operators and the load balancer must be able to tell 'process up' from 'able to serve': /ready should fail when the database or the audit chain is unhealthy.
constraints: No production deploy inside this mission
approval_rules: Production deployment is a separate critical action with change, rollback, and verification plans

tasks.title: Design note: /ready semantics and failure modes

params.title: Readiness probe design
params.problem: /health only proves the process is running. Traffic should drain when the store or the audit chain cannot be trusted.
decisions: /health stays a liveness probe with no dependencies
/ready runs a database round-trip and an audit-chain head check
/ready returns 503 with a machine-readable reason and never leaks internals
acceptance_criteria: /ready returns 200 when the store and audit chain are healthy
/ready returns 503 when the database is unreachable
/ready returns 503 when the audit chain fails verification
/ready responds in under 250 ms on a healthy instance
Neither probe requires authentication or returns secrets

files.change: Add a /ready route that calls office.readiness() and maps failures to 503.
Add readiness(): SELECT 1 on the store, then verify the audit-chain head.
Cover healthy, database-down, and tampered-chain cases.

tasks.title: Test plan from the acceptance criteria
Review the patch against the test plan

missions.title: Authority week: three plain-language posts for Ontario operators
missions.objective: Publish useful, sourced content that answers real questions local owners ask about cyber and AI risk.
deliverables: One post submitted for publishing approval
constraints: No invented statistics, clients, results, or quotes
End every post with one concrete next step
approval_rules: Publishing is a high-risk external action and needs operator approval

posts.topic: Before you connect an AI assistant to client files
points: List which folders and mailboxes the tool can read
Check where the vendor stores and processes that data
Decide who can switch the connection off, and test it
posts.next_step: Write down the three answers before you sign up.

posts.topic: What an approval gate is and why your automations need one
points: Anything that sends, pays, publishes, or deletes waits for a named person
Every approval records who decided and why
posts.next_step: Pick one automation this week and add a human sign-off step.

posts.topic: The first hour after a phishing click
points: Disconnect the device from the network, do not wipe it
Reset the password from a different device
Write down the time, the message, and what was clicked
posts.next_step: Print these three steps and tape them near the office printer.
